curated.conceptDesc: Multi-tenant cloud platform delivering software instantly via browser with automated overnight updates.
curated.oneLiner: Software you rent and use through a web browser — no install, no IT department. Now evolving into Smart Apps that do the work for you.
curated.notes: SaaS replaced buying software on discs. Smart Apps are now replacing the need to click through it manually.
curated.origin: Salesforce & SIIA (2000) · Evolving → AI-Enabled Smart Apps (2025+)

smartStack.label: AI-Enabled Smart Apps
smartStack.headline: SaaS is becoming the Smart Stack
smartStack.description: For 20 years SaaS meant: rent software, click through menus, repeat. The shift happening right now: you describe what you want in plain language and the Smart App handles every step. The technical part vanishes. What stays is your intention — and the outcome.

legacyStack.label: Click a menu to do a thing
legacyStack.note: 50 screens. Manual. Every step requires a trained human.

legacyStack.label: Per-seat licensing
legacyStack.note: You pay for access. Whether anyone uses it or not.

legacyStack.label: You are the workflow
legacyStack.note: If you stop clicking, nothing happens.

legacyStack.label: IT owns the update cycle
legacyStack.note: Quarterly patches. You wait. They schedule.

newStack.label: Describe what you want
newStack.note: Plain language. No training required. The Smart App understands intent.

newStack.label: Pay for the outcome
newStack.note: Value-based. You pay for what gets done, not who has a login.

newStack.label: Agents are the workflow
newStack.note: They plan, execute, verify, and report back. You review the result.

newStack.label: The app improves itself
newStack.note: Every run makes it smarter. No manual update cycle.

anatomy.desc: A program — now evolving from static screens you click to AI agents that work for you.
Delivered through the internet. You open a browser. It's there. No installation, no server room.
Like a subscription — Netflix for business software. Cancel anytime. No large upfront costs.

flow.title: User Goal / Intent
flow.desc: User expresses high-level goal in natural language or voice.

flow.title: Smart App Brain
flow.desc: Autonomous AI agents plan tasks and inspect live data.

flow.title: Agent Execution
flow.desc: Swarm executes tools, generates assets, and verifies output.

flow.title: Completed Value $$
flow.desc: Finished deliverables published with zero manual grunt work.

senses.definition: A software licensing and delivery model in which applications are hosted by a provider and made available to customers over a network, typically the internet, on a subscription or pay-per-use basis.
examples: Many startups choose a saas model to reduce upfront infrastructure costs and accelerate deployment.
The university migrated its email system to a saas solution managed by an external vendor.

senses.definition: A business or revenue model in which value is delivered primarily through ongoing access to remotely hosted software, usually involving recurring billing, service-level agreements, and continuous updates.
examples: Investors often favor saas companies because their recurring revenues are more predictable than traditional license sales.
From a strategic perspective, saas alters incentives by tying vendor profits to long-term customer retention rather than one-time transactions.

senses.definition: An individual product, platform, or company that operates according to the software as a service model, often contrasted with platform as a service or infrastructure as a service.
examples: The research compares a traditional enterprise resource planning system with a cloud-native saas in terms of total cost of ownership.
The firm offers multiple cloud services, including iaas, paas, and a flagship saas for data analytics.
